title: 5 Best Proton VPN Alternatives in 2026, Compared
summary: Which Proton VPN alternative you choose depends on whether you value speed, price, or independence from a single vendor's ecosystem.
body_markdown:
## IVPN as a Proton VPN alternative


If you want to check a privacy claim yourself rather than take it on trust, IVPN is built for that. It does so through published pricing, audit reports and open-source apps.


Start with pricing, since that's where it departs from the previous provider. According to ivpn.net, IVPN sells a short list of plans that differ mainly in how many devices can connect at once and which advanced networking features come with them.


There's no free tier to fall back on and no long ladder of bundled extras. The cost is easy to read, but a reader who left Proton VPN because they wanted to pay nothing won't find that option here.


### IVPN audits and open-source apps


Read the no-logs claim second. IVPN states on its site that it doesn't record traffic, connection timestamps or the IP addresses of the people using the service.


A statement like that is only as good as the evidence behind it, so the more useful point is that **IVPN publishes independent audit reports** .


The reports cover what the auditors reviewed at the time, not what happens on the servers today, so treat them as evidence about the setup rather than a standing guarantee.


Anyone can read the code that runs on your device, because the apps are open source. For a technical user that means a claim about client behaviour can be checked against the source, and a non-technical user can rely on others having done so.


### The trade-offs of that transparency


In exchange for that transparency, you accept some limits. IVPN runs a smaller server footprint than the larger commercial providers in this comparison, so users who need a server in a specific or remote country should check the location list first.


The apps are also plainer. They lean toward clear settings over the streamlined, consumer-friendly polish of the bigger names.


That makes IVPN the better fit for readers whose complaint about Proton VPN was a lack of verifiable detail. It's a weaker fit for those who left over price or for a wide server map.


Being able to leave is the same test for a workflow tool, and[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) passes it: Git Sync and Releases is a documented feature in its docs, so a flow built on the managed cloud can be promoted and moved to a self-hosted install, which runs through Docker, Compose or Kubernetes on the same codebase.


Self-hosting is an edition you can actually choose, so the exit stays open however good your flows are. RBAC, SSO, SCIM and audit logs come with both deployments, and MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run it in production.


Where it runs should never decide whether you can leave, and the same goes for a tunnel.
